subject: PHS
vignette: A surgical oncology team follows 120 patients for 5 years after pancreatectomy and constructs a graphic display in which the estimated probability of remaining alive is shown on the y-axis and the length of time since surgery on the x-axis, with stepwise downward ticks each time a death occurs.
question: Which of the following best describes this graphic representation?

options.text: It plots the number of new cases of disease over time on the y-axis, estimating incidence.
It is restricted to mortality outcomes and cannot be used for any other type of event.
It estimates the proportion of the population with the disease at each point in time, estimating prevalence.
It is a Kaplan-Meier curve estimating the probability of survival over time for time-to-event data, where survival probability = 1 − event probability.
It plots the instantaneous hazard of death on the y-axis, and the curve can only descend toward zero.

explanation_correct: This is a Kaplan-Meier curve, used to estimate the probability of survival over time: the y-axis shows survival probabilities and the x-axis shows the length of time, making it the standard display for time-to-event data. The survival probability equals 1 − event probability. Although the event is frequently mortality, outcomes examined may include any event, such as recurrence or graft failure.

explanation_incorrect.A: Counting new cases over time measures incidence, not survival; the Kaplan-Meier y-axis is a probability of remaining event-free, not a case count.
explanation_incorrect.B: Although mortality is the most frequent outcome examined, a Kaplan-Meier analysis can be used for any defined event, including recurrence or cure.
explanation_incorrect.C: Estimating the proportion of a population with disease at a point in time measures prevalence; the Kaplan-Meier curve estimates the probability of surviving (remaining event-free) over follow-up time.
explanation_incorrect.E: The y-axis of a Kaplan-Meier curve is the survival probability (starting at 1.0 and stepping downward), not the instantaneous hazard, and the description of an ascending-only constraint is incorrect.

educationalObjective: A Kaplan-Meier curve displays survival probability (y-axis) versus time (x-axis) for time-to-event data, with survival probability = 1 − event probability.

subject: PHS
vignette: A cohort study of patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction reports that over 3 years of follow-up, the probability of the composite event (death or transplant) is 1 in 4. The investigators now wish to display these data as a Kaplan-Meier survival curve.
question: What value should be plotted as the 3-year survival probability on the y-axis of the curve?
explanation_correct: On a Kaplan-Meier curve, survival probability = 1 − event probability. An event probability of 1 in 4 (25%) therefore corresponds to a 3-year survival probability of 1 − 0.25 = 0.75, or 75%, which is the value plotted at the 3-year time point on the y-axis.

explanation_incorrect.B: 25% is the event probability itself, not the survival probability; the curve plots the complement.
explanation_incorrect.C: 33% results from inverting the event fraction (1/3), which is not related to either the event or the survival probability.
explanation_incorrect.D: 67% comes from subtracting the inverted fraction (1 − 33%), compounding the inversion error; the survival probability is 1 − 25%.
explanation_incorrect.E: 50% has no basis in the reported event probability; it neither follows from 1 − 25% nor from the event rate itself.

educationalObjective: Survival probability = 1 − event probability, the value plotted on the y-axis of a Kaplan-Meier curve.

subject: PHS
vignette: A randomized trial compares two anticoagulation regimens after mechanical heart valve replacement and displays the freedom-from-embolism probability for each group as Kaplan-Meier curves over 4 years. The curves visibly diverge, and the investigators want to report a p value for the difference in survival between the two groups.
question: Which of the following statistical approaches is appropriate for calculating this p value?

options.text: A paired t-test comparing the mean event-free times of the two groups.
The log-rank test comparing the two survival curves.
A Pearson correlation coefficient between time and event status.
A one-way ANOVA comparing mean survival across the treatment groups.
A chi-square test comparing the 4-year incidence rates only.

explanation_correct: The p value for the difference between two Kaplan-Meier survival curves is calculated using the log-rank test (or Cox regression). These methods use the full time-to-event information, including censored observations, rather than collapsing follow-up to a single time point or a mean.

explanation_incorrect.A: A paired t-test requires paired, normally distributed measurements and ignores censoring; it is not the method for comparing two survival curves.
explanation_incorrect.C: A Pearson correlation quantifies the linear association between two continuous variables; it does not test the difference between two survival distributions with censored data.
explanation_incorrect.D: ANOVA compares means among groups and is unsuitable for time-to-event data subject to censoring, which survival methods are designed to handle.
explanation_incorrect.E: Comparing incidence rates at a single 4-year time point discards the timing of events and the censored follow-up; survival comparison uses the log-rank test or Cox regression.

educationalObjective: The p value for the difference between survival curves is calculated using the log-rank test or Cox regression.

subject: PHS
vignette: In a trial of a new drug versus placebo after myocardial infarction, the drug group's Kaplan-Meier curve remains above the placebo curve at every time point during 2 years of follow-up. During the study, several patients in both groups move away and are lost to follow-up, and some are still alive and event-free when the study ends.
question: Which of the following statements is most accurate regarding the interpretation of these Kaplan-Meier curves?

options.text: Patients lost to follow-up should be counted as deaths at the time they leave the study.
The analysis cannot be completed unless every patient experiences the event before the study ends.
The downward steps in the curve represent the prevalence of the disease at each time point.
Because patients were censored, the difference between the curves cannot be formally tested.
Censored patients contribute follow-up time until their last observation, and the sustained separation of the curves can be tested with the log-rank test.

explanation_correct: Kaplan-Meier analysis is designed for time-to-event data with censored observations: patients who are lost to follow-up or event-free at study end contribute survival time up to their last known observation and are then removed from further risk, without being counted as events. A curve that remains above another at all time points indicates a higher survival probability in that group, and the difference can be formally tested with the log-rank test or Cox regression.

explanation_incorrect.A: Censored patients are not assumed to have had the event; counting losses as deaths would falsely inflate mortality and violate the method's handling of incomplete follow-up.
explanation_incorrect.B: A Kaplan-Meier curve can be constructed with censored data — that is precisely its purpose; requiring every subject to reach the endpoint would eliminate the need for survival analysis.
explanation_incorrect.C: The downward steps represent event occurrences that lower the survival probability; prevalence is the number of existing cases in a population and is not plotted on this curve.
explanation_incorrect.D: Censoring is routinely handled by survival methods; the log-rank test (or Cox regression) formally tests the difference between curves despite censored observations.

educationalObjective: In Kaplan-Meier analysis, censored patients contribute survival time until their last observation, and curve differences are tested with the log-rank test or Cox regression.
